usageNotes: Use this to register a VM or container with the Proxmox HA manager so the cluster can automatically start, restart, and migrate it when nodes fail. The target resource (VM or CT) must already exist on a cluster node before adding it to HA — the HA manager does not create resources. Requires the 'Sys.Console' privilege at the root path, so only cluster administrators can add HA resources.

examples.summary: Enable HA for VM 105, pinned to group 'production', with failback on

tips: The 'sid' shorthand (e.g. '105') resolves to 'vm:105' or 'ct:105' automatically, but using the explicit form avoids ambiguity when VM and CT IDs overlap.

Setting 'state' to 'stopped' at creation is useful for registering a resource without immediately letting the HA manager start it — helpful when you want HA tracking but control the first start manually.
The 'group' field references an HA group created via POST /cluster/ha/groups; omit it to let the HA manager use any available node.

After creating the resource, verify it appears with GET /cluster/ha/resources and that the 'status' field transitions from 'fence' or 'recovery' to 'started' within a few seconds on a healthy cluster.
auto-rebalance defaults to true (1); set it to false on latency-sensitive workloads to prevent unexpected live migrations during routine cluster rebalancing.
